title: Heitor Villa-Lobos's birth chart
metaDescription: Heitor Villa-Lobos's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.8° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 16.7° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 14.8° Pisces — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that the Moon, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 2.9° Aries; Venus stands at 6.7° Aries; Mars stands at 26.1° Pisces. The tradition reads thought that arrives already in motion from Mercury, attraction declared rather than implied from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.7°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Mars sextile Neptune at 0.8°, and the Sun trine Saturn at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Jupiter makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. The Moon in Cancer at 16.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Aries at 6.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Cancer at 15.7° is in detriment. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in water, 2 in fire, 2 in air, 1 in earth by element, 5 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 16.7°.
